claims.claim: The Israeli postal code (mikud) is 7 digits and is resolved per address, not per city, through the Israel Post lookup form. The form asks for locality, then street within that locality, then house number. There is no keyless public API: see the israel-post-mikud claim for the 401-versus-404 test that establishes the backing endpoint is auth-gated rather than dead.
claims.raw_snippet: איתור המיקוד לפי: כתובת ת.ד יישוב
claims.verified_via: browser, page text read with location.href asserted; the site is Radware bot-gated so curl returns an undifferentiated SPA shell and is not a valid check for this host
claims.source_note: The page is client-rendered; read in Playwright with location.href asserted.

claims.claim: Israel Post's mikud lookup is the web form at doar.israelpost.co.il/locatezip. The site is backed by a JSON API on apimftprd.israelpost.co.il that requires a subscription key: calling it without one returns HTTP 401 with the message that the subscription key is missing, while an undefined sibling path on the same host returns HTTP 404, so the host discriminates and the 401 is a real auth gate rather than a dead endpoint. There is therefore no keyless public mikud-by-address API.
claims.raw_snippet: { "statusCode": 401, "message": "Access denied due to missing subscription key. Make sure to include subscription key when making requests to an API." }
claims.verified_via: curl, with an undefined sibling path returning 404 as a negative control

claims.claim: api.govmap.gov.il serves a developer DOCUMENTATION site, not a callable REST endpoint. GovMap is delivered as a JavaScript SDK (govmap.api.js), and its functions require a valid API key sent from an APPROVED DOMAIN on every call, so it cannot be driven from a CLI or a server-side agent. The documentation entry point is https://api.govmap.gov.il/docs/intro and the standalone-usage page carrying the API-key requirement is https://api.govmap.gov.il/docs/intro/standalone.
claims.raw_snippet: השימוש בפונקציות אינו מחייב יצירת מפה, אך מחייב שליחת מפתח API תקף, מהדומיין המאושר, בכל קריאה

claims.claim: The Survey of Israel block/parcel-by-address (gush/helka) tool is at gov.il/apps/mapi/parcel_address/parcel_address.html. The host is Cloudflare-protected and returns HTTP 403 to curl, and the 403 body is identical for a nonsense sibling path, so curl cannot confirm the specific page. It renders for a human in a browser. Treat this as a human-facing tool, not an agent-callable endpoint.
claims.verified_via: browser render; curl returns an undifferentiated 403 Cloudflare block whose body is byte-identical for a nonsense sibling path, so curl is not a valid check for this host

claims.claim: data.gov.il exposes a keyless public CKAN API. The settlements dataset resource_id is 5c78e9fa-c2e2-4771-93ff-7f400a12f7ba and holds 1,310 records with fields סמל_ישוב, שם_ישוב and שם_נפה. The streets dataset resource_id is 9ad3862c-8391-4b2f-84a4-2d4c68625f4b with fields סמל_ישוב, שם_ישוב, סמל_רחוב and שם_רחוב. Both datasets are published by רשות האוכלוסין וההגירה. A bad resource_id returns an HTML error page rather than JSON.
claims.verified_via: curl, 1310 records returned, bogus resource_id returns HTTP 404 as a negative control

claims.claim: Israel Post's lookup form addresses localities and streets by internal ids that are NOT the semel yishuv or the semel rechov. After selecting תל אביב - יפו in the locality field, the form's own requests carry CityID=1212, while the semel yishuv for that locality is 5000. The internal ids are only observable from the form's network traffic, because the endpoint itself is subscription-key gated. Passing a semel yishuv where the internal city id is expected returns an empty result with no error.
claims.verified_via: browser: observed in the live network trace of doar.israelpost.co.il/locatezip with location.href asserted, after selecting תל אביב - יפו. The endpoint returns HTTP 401 without the site's subscription key, so the value cannot be re-checked by a direct call; the evidence is the request the site itself issues.
